T-001.Title: Deterministic discard preflight, recovery preservation, and final behavior tests

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: `src/grace-cursor.ts` reconciles the prospective stream against the durable ledger **before** validating allocation/density: pure or partial recorded residue resumes and is never re-validated as a fresh set; a mixed residue-plus-fresh set validates only the events that are actually fresh; a genuine payload conflict and an older-epoch id reuse refuse before the `discarded` write; an invalid fresh stream refuses before any write. The too-narrow-allocation row (the `F158` reproduction), the duplicate-event-id row (the `F292.1` measurement), the pre-existing-range-hole row, and the no-allocation `{1:progress, 3:progress}` stream each refuse with the complete recursive project tree byte-identical (added, changed, and deleted paths), no `*-discarded.xml`, no synthesized `opened`, and a byte-identical `run-ledger.xml` when it exists. The positive control repairs uniqueness and preserves density/allocation validity, folds through the real product path, writes exactly one `discarded`, folds it once, and empties `run/`; the no-loose-events state remains a no-op that writes nothing.

The recovery-preservation arm is driven through the changed caller and the real CLI: a partial-deletion residue hole (`{1:opened, 3:terminal}` exactly matching the durable last epoch) and a mixed residue-plus-fresh set each resume through `discardAndFoldEpoch`; the real CLI `ngrace supersede --change C-OLD --replacement C-OLD-2` archives the predecessor from each. The prior epoch stays byte-identical, and each recorded ledger's complete event population, attributes, and child text/children equal an independently derived expected set (the captured epoch-1 and fresh events plus the engine's synthetic `discarded` and covering `opened`, with bounds derived from the captured ids and the shipped headroom), never an expected built from the resulting ledger.

The bounded competing-writer seam is driven: after a successful preflight snapshot a controlled non-cooperating actor adds a deterministic conflicting event, the operation writes exactly one pre-ledger `discarded` residue and refuses before any ledger write, and the actor then reverses only its own mutation. A real `bun run ngrace cursor fold` retry consumes the preserved `discarded` exactly once unchanged (its captured pre-retry payload equals the recorded payload) and the recorded ledger's complete population, attributes, and children equal the projection of the captured pre-retry loose population, built independently of the result, with `run/` empty. This stage-(ii-a) outcome is explicitly not a stage-(i) preflight-snapshot outcome and not the distinct post-ledger `C-RUN-LEDGER` boundary.

The final repository tests are landed first and re-driven on the approved base for behavioral red before the production change. With the identical final test file on base and candidate: the base shows the four deterministic-residue directions, the missing-seam direction, and the structural `AC-DISCARDED-CALLER` pin direction classified separately, and the candidate is green. All bundle-1/2/3/4 controls stay green: vanished-entry tolerance, malformed closer/progress refusal, pure residue, partial deletion, genuine conflict, older-epoch reuse, mixed success and `F_bad`, both mixed hooks, both original hooks, and the idempotent third empty retry. `src/grace-cursor.ts` adds no new `unlinkSync` site; the `kind: "discarded"` literal count is re-measured and pinned to the final implementation.
